9297190.headline: Caherdavin Pupils Bring Color and Song to Na Piarsaigh's Final Preparations
9297190.subheadline: Christ the King National School shows unwavering support ahead of Limerick Senior Hurling Championship showdown.
9297190.story:
Excitement reached fever pitch in Caherdavin this week as the corridors of Christ the King National School transformed into a sea of light blue and dark blue. Pupils and staff alike rallied behind their local heroes, Na Piarsaigh, as the club prepares for another momentous appearance in the Limerick Senior Hurling Championship final.

Classrooms were adorned with homemade banners, flags, and pennants bearing messages of encouragement for the players. The children gathered in the schoolyard to voice their support, showcasing a deep-rooted passion for the club that spans generations within the local community. For many of the young supporters, seeing familiar faces from their neighborhood pull on the famous jersey is a source of immense pride and inspiration.

Local sporting fixtures of this magnitude consistently serve to unite communities across Limerick, fostering a shared sense of identity and civic pride. The enthusiasm displayed by the students at Christ the King highlights the vital role that local clubs play not only in athletic development, but in anchoring community spirit among the younger generation as they look forward to a memorable weekend of hurling action.
9297190.pullQuote: The enthusiasm displayed by the students at Christ the King highlights the vital role that local clubs play in anchoring community spirit.
9297190.localAngle: The vibrant show of support from Christ the King students underscores the deep community ties driving Na Piarsaigh ahead of the Limerick Senior Hurling Championship final.
9297190.originalTitle: PICTURES: Limerick school cheers on their team ahead of county final

9299281.headline: Community Bids Fond Farewell to Castletroy Stalwart Known for Warmth and Generosity
9299281.subheadline: Friends, family, and fellow club members gather to celebrate the life of a cherished local figure.
9299281.story:
The Limerick community turned out in large numbers this week to pay their final respects to a widely known and deeply respected local man, remembered fondly by all who knew him as a source of constant kindness and charm. Mourners gathered to celebrate a life defined by quiet generosity and an unwavering commitment to enriching the lives of those around him.

Among the hardest hit by the loss are members of the Castletroy Golf Club, where the popular Limerick resident was a foundational pillar of the community. For years, he dedicated his time, talents, and boundless energy to the club, playing an instrumental role in its daily life and fostering enduring friendships on and off the course.

While his passing leaves a noticeable void in the hearts of his family and friends, the overwhelming sentiment shared across Limerick is one of immense gratitude for the positivity he brought to the area. His legacy of warmth, community spirit, and genuine care for others will continue to inspire those who had the privilege of crossing paths with him.
9299281.pullQuote: Such a lovely, kind, charming person who gave so much of his time and talents to our community.
9299281.localAngle: The life and legacy of a beloved Castletroy Golf Club member is celebrated by the wider Limerick community.
9299281.originalTitle: RIP: ’Such a lovely, kind, charming person’- Popular Limerick man is laid to rest

9300202.headline: Treaty County Rugby Clubs Gear Up as AIL Action Resumes This Weekend
9300202.subheadline: All seven Limerick men's sides return to the pitch following a brief fortnight break, promising an action-packed weekend of domestic rugby.
9300202.story:
Rugby enthusiasts across the Treaty County are in for a treat this weekend as the All-Ireland League (AIL) roars back to life following a two-week hiatus. The brief break has allowed squads to regroup, recover from early-season knocks, and fine-tune their strategies as the 2026/27 campaign begins to take shape.

All seven of Limerick's men's sides will be in competitive action, bringing a renewed sense of anticipation and community spirit to grounds across the city and county. Local clubs have reported strong preparations during the break, with coaches and players eager to showcase their progress and secure vital league points in front of passionate home and traveling supporters.

The return of full-scale AIL fixtures serves as a vital anchor for the local sporting calendar, driving footfall and fostering a strong sense of camaraderie among players, volunteers, and fans alike. As the season enters this crucial phase, the resilience and dedication displayed by clubs at all levels highlight the enduring strength of Limerick's rich rugby tradition.
9300202.pullQuote: All seven Men’s sides from the Treaty County will be back in action this weekend after a two-week hiatus.
9300202.localAngle: The return of all seven Limerick men's sides to AIL competition highlights the county's vibrant rugby culture and strong community engagement.
9300202.originalTitle: AIL action returns to Limerick following two-week hiatus

9300204.headline: Treaty United Women Ready to Write Final Chapter of Historic 2026 Campaign on Home Turf
9300204.subheadline: Limerick side prepares for emotional season finale against DLR Waves at Markets Field this evening.
9300204.story:
Treaty United’s women’s team is set to bring down the curtain on a landmark SSE Airtricity Premier Division campaign this evening, welcoming DLR Waves to Limerick for a 5pm kickoff. The fixture marks the culmination of months of dedication, growth, and competitive football that has continued to capture the imagination of local sports enthusiasts throughout the region.

As the squad prepares to step onto the pitch for the final time this season, players and coaching staff alike are reflecting on the progress made over the past several months. The team has consistently demonstrated resilience and determination, representing Limerick proudly on the national stage and inspiring the next generation of young players coming through local grassroots clubs across the county.

Supporters are expected to turn out in strong numbers to show their appreciation for the squad's efforts this season. Tonight’s match is not only the final fixture on the calendar but also an opportunity to celebrate a positive trajectory for women's football in the region, paving the way for even greater achievements when the team returns to action in the future.
9300204.pullQuote: The Treaty United women's side is ready to finish their 2026 campaign in style in front of home supporters.
9300204.localAngle: The match at Markets Field offers Limerick sports fans a final chance this season to support their local Premier Division women's team.
9300204.originalTitle: Treaty United Women aim to finish season as history makers

9300781.headline: Red Army Gears Up as Munster Shifts Focus to Leinster Showdown
9300781.subheadline: Building on recent momentum, the province prepares for a thrilling inter-provincial clash following a stellar 31-14 victory.
9300781.story:
Munster rugby supporters across Limerick and the wider province are turning their attention to the upcoming inter-provincial challenge as preparations ramp up for a high-stakes fixture against Leinster. Following a string of encouraging performances and a decisive 31-14 victory in the corresponding fixture last season, the squad is eager to maintain their upward trajectory in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

Head coach and players have been putting in rigorous work on the training ground, aiming to harness the positive energy from recent outings to deliver another memorable performance for the passionate home faithful. The upcoming match offers an ideal platform for the team to showcase their tactical growth, depth, and resilience against formidable opposition.

For the local community, fixtures against Leinster always carry a special significance, uniting fans in pubs, clubs, and Thomond Park to celebrate the spirit of the game. As the province builds towards kick-off, the collective optimism surrounding the team highlights the enduring connection between Munster Rugby and the people of Limerick, promising an electrifying atmosphere for all in attendance.
9300781.pullQuote: Munster are looking to build on recent positive performances as they prepare for a crucial Leinster trip.
9300781.localAngle: Limerick supporters are rallying behind Munster as the squad prepares for a high-stakes URC clash against Leinster.
9300781.originalTitle: Leinster trip next up for improving Munster as focus switches to URC

9301758.headline: Kilmallock District Court Delivers Verdict in Bruff Garda Station Assault Case
9301758.subheadline: Local legal proceedings highlight ongoing dedication to supporting emergency services across County Limerick.
9301758.story:
The Kilmallock District Court has concluded a notable legal proceeding regarding an assault on a member of An Garda Síochána at Bruff Garda Station. The case, which drew local attention, underscores the critical role that district courts play in upholding the rule of law and maintaining public safety throughout County Limerick.

Legal proceedings of this nature reaffirm the unwavering commitment of local authorities to protect frontline workers and ensure that community spaces remain safe for both residents and the personnel who serve them. An Garda Síochána continues to work collaboratively with communities across the region to foster mutual respect, safety, and constructive civic engagement.

As County Limerick communities continue to thrive through strong neighborhood initiatives and cooperative public safety efforts, local leaders emphasize the importance of constructive dialogue and support for emergency personnel. The resolution of this case at Kilmallock marks another step in upholding the high standards of justice and community well-being that define the region.
9301758.pullQuote: The case highlights the dedication of frontline workers and the judicial system in maintaining community safety across County Limerick.
9301758.localAngle: The hearing at Kilmallock District Court addresses local law enforcement matters concerning Bruff Garda Station in County Limerick.
9301758.originalTitle: Conviction for woman who assaulted a garda in Limerick station

9302767.headline: Neighbour Rivalry Set to Ignite TUS Gaelic Grounds in Premier Intermediate Decider
9302767.subheadline: Dromin-Athlacca and Bruff prepare for a high-stakes hurling showdown this Sunday afternoon.
9302767.story:
Anticipation has reached fever pitch across South Limerick this week as local communities gear up for one of the most compelling fixtures of the club hurling calendar. Dromin-Athlacca are set to face their close neighbours Bruff this Sunday at the TUS Gaelic Grounds in the Lyons of Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship Final, with both sides eager to claim the ultimate prize.

For Dromin-Athlacca, the fixture represents an opportunity of significant magnitude. The squad has shown remarkable resilience and dedication throughout the 2026 campaign, positioning themselves firmly on the doorstep of an immediate return to the senior ranks. Their journey to the final reflects the hard work taking place at club level, where players, coaches, and volunteers have poured their energy into fostering a competitive and supportive sporting environment.

Meanwhile, Bruff head into Sunday's showdown carrying their own proud traditions and strong community backing, ensuring that the atmosphere at headquarters will be nothing short of electrifying. Both sets of supporters are expected to turn out in large numbers to paint the stands in their club colours, showcasing the vibrant community spirit that remains the beating heart of Limerick hurling.

Throw-in at the TUS Gaelic Grounds is sure to draw a passionate crowd as two proud parishes lock horns for county glory. Beyond the silverwear, Sunday's decider is a celebration of grassroots sport and the unifying power of hurling across the county, promising a sporting spectacle that fans will remember for seasons to come.
9302767.pullQuote: Dromin-Athlacca are preparing for a Lyons of Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship Final clash with neighbours Bruff this Sunday at TUS Gaelic Grounds.
9302767.localAngle: This high-profile local derby at the TUS Gaelic Grounds highlights the vibrant community spirit and fierce sporting passion defining club hurling across County Limerick.
9302767.originalTitle: Dromin-Athlacca hoping to return to the senior grade at first attempt

9305835.headline: Sisters Injured in M9 Tragedy Express Deep Gratitude Amid Remarkable Recovery
9305835.subheadline: Ella, Niamh, and Alma share a message of thanks following the devastating August collision.
9305835.story:
Three Limerick sisters who sustained critical injuries in a devastating two-vehicle collision on the M9 motorway in August have spoken publicly for the first time, expressing their profound gratitude for the outpouring of local support that has sustained their ongoing recovery. Ella, Niamh, and Alma were among those severely injured in the tragic incident that deeply affected communities across the region.

In a heartfelt message released this week, the sisters shared their appreciation for the tireless efforts of emergency services, medical staff, and the wider community who rallied around their families during the darkest days following the crash. Their message reflects a spirit of resilience and hope as they continue to make strides in their rehabilitation, surrounded by the unwavering encouragement of loved ones and neighbors.

The August collision remains a somber memory for the community, having also claimed the lives of five teenage boys in a tragedy that sent shockwaves nationwide. As the families affected continue to heal, the courage and solidarity shown by the community stand as a testament to the strength and compassion inherent in the region during times of profound challenge.
9305835.pullQuote: Our hearts remain full of gratitude for the incredible support that has carried us through every step of our recovery.
9305835.localAngle: The resilience of the three Limerick sisters highlights the profound community spirit and mutual support present throughout the county during times of healing.
9305835.originalTitle: 'Forever grateful' -  Sisters injured in horror M9 crash share heartfelt message

9306638.headline: Limerick's Scarlett Faulkner Remembered in Special Prayers at St. Peter's Basilica
9306638.subheadline: Family's heartfelt Italian pilgrimage brings local hope and solidarity to the heart of the Vatican.
9306638.story:
The thoughts and prayers of the local community traveled far beyond the Treaty County this week, as young Scarlett Faulkner and her brother, Jason, became the focal point of a special devotional gathering at the Vatican in Rome.

Family members undertaking a pilgrimage to Italy ensured that the Limerick siblings remained at the forefront of their minds throughout the journey. The gesture of solidarity and hope highlights the enduring strength of family bonds and the powerful ways in which local networks extend their support across international borders.

Back home in Limerick, the gesture has resonated warmly among friends and neighbors who continue to rally around the Faulkner family. Moments like these reflect the deep-rooted community spirit and resilience that define our local neighborhoods, offering a profound sense of shared encouragement and optimism for the future.
9306638.pullQuote: Siblings Scarlett and Jason Faulkner were in the forefront of family members’ minds during pilgrimage to Italy.
9306638.localAngle: Limerick siblings Scarlett and Jason Faulkner were specially prayed for by local family members during a pilgrimage to the Vatican in Rome.
9306638.originalTitle: Limerick’s Scarlett Faulkner prayed for at the Vatican

9307165.headline: Minister O'Donovan Champions Workplace Inclusion for People with Disabilities
9307165.subheadline: Limerick representative aims to pave the way for greater government diversity
9307165.story:
Minister Patrick O'Donovan has stepped forward with a clear message regarding workplace inclusivity, expressing his strong commitment to demonstrating that individuals living with a disability or neurological condition can thrive at the highest levels of government. Speaking publicly on the matter, the Limerick-based minister emphasized the importance of representation and breaking down traditional barriers that have often kept marginalized groups out of public service roles.

The initiative has been met with widespread encouragement from local advocates and community leaders across Limerick, who view the move as a significant step toward a more accessible and representative public sector. By sharing his perspective, O'Donovan aims to foster an environment where ability is defined by capability and dedication rather than preconceptions, encouraging both public and private sector employers to re-evaluate their own hiring practices.

Local disability support networks have praised the constructive dialogue sparked by the Limerick minister's comments, noting that visible leadership plays a crucial role in inspiring the next generation of workers. As conversations around workplace accessibility continue to evolve, this development highlights a growing momentum toward creating truly inclusive spaces where every citizen has the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society.
9307165.pullQuote: Minister O'Donovan wants to show that people with a disability or neurological condition can successfully work in government.
9307165.localAngle: Limerick Minister Patrick O'Donovan leads national dialogue on workplace accessibility and government representation.
9307165.originalTitle: EDITORIAL: 'Patrick O'Donovan has courage to speak out while others whisper'

9307472.headline: Doon Eyes Glory in Premier Junior Hurling Decider
9307472.subheadline: East Limerick club looks to capitalize on big-match experience ahead of weekend final
9307472.story:
Anticipation has reached fever pitch across East Limerick this week as the Doon club prepares for a monumental weekend on the hurling field. The squad is leaving no stone unturned in their quest for silverware in the Premier Junior Hurling final, aiming to take that crucial final step after knocking loudly on the door of championship success.

Adding significant firepower to the forward line is Darragh Stapleton, whose composure and proven track record on the big stage will be vital. Having already tested himself at the highest level—including a stellar appearance in last year’s Senior Hurling Championship final—Stapleton is expected to anchor the attack from center forward, bringing invaluable tactical awareness and leadership to the young and ambitious side.

Club officials and supporters alike have praised the dedication of the players and coaching staff, who have fostered a remarkable sense of unity and resilience throughout the campaign. Win or lose, the journey to the final stands as a testament to the thriving underage structures and community spirit that continue to make Doon a proud powerhouse of Limerick hurling.
9307472.pullQuote: Darragh Stapleton is expected to line out at center forward, bringing invaluable big-match experience to the Doon attack.
9307472.localAngle: The upcoming Premier Junior Hurling final highlights the strong sporting traditions and community pride deeply embedded in East Limerick.
9307472.originalTitle: Doon looking to go one better in Premier Junior Hurling final

9307476.headline: Third Time's the Charm: Bruree Prepares for Redemption on County Final Day
9307476.subheadline: South Limerick side channels years of hard work and resilience into Sunday's Intermediate Hurling Championship showdown.
9307476.story:
The village of Bruree is buzzing with anticipation this weekend as the local intermediate hurling team prepares to make its third consecutive appearance in the county final. Having narrowly missed out on the ultimate prize in each of the past two seasons, the squad has channeled the heartbreak of those previous campaigns into a renewed sense of purpose and unity.

Throughout the current season, the team has demonstrated remarkable resilience, showcasing the strong community spirit and dedication that defines local sports in south Limerick. Coaches, players, and supporters have worked tirelessly behind the scenes, focusing on youth development and tactical preparation to ensure the club reaches its full potential on the big stage.

Win or lose, Sunday's match represents a celebration of local pride and athletic achievement. The entire community has rallied behind the players, decorating streets in the club's colors and coming together to support a group of athletes who embody the very best of Limerick's rich hurling tradition.
9307476.pullQuote: Having narrowly missed out on the ultimate prize in each of the past two seasons, the squad has channeled the heartbreak of those previous campaigns into a renewed sense of purpose and unity.
9307476.localAngle: This gripping county final appearance highlights the vibrant club hurling culture and unwavering community spirit across south Limerick.

9307685.headline: Bank Holiday Bonanza: Lucky Limerick Ticket Holder Claims Half-Million EuroMillions Prize
9307685.subheadline: National Lottery officials urge players across the county to check their numbers following Friday night's massive draw.
9307685.story:
There is a buzz of excitement across the Treaty County this weekend as National Lottery officials confirm that a single ticket holder in Limerick has won a staggering €500,000 in the EuroMillions draw. The life-changing win is expected to set the stage for an unforgettable Bank Holiday weekend for the yet-unnamed lucky participant.

While the exact location where the winning ticket was purchased has not yet been revealed by lottery headquarters, anticipation is already building in local shops and communities. National Lottery spokesperson Emma Monaghan shared the thrilling news on Saturday morning, encouraging everyone who participated in Friday's draw to thoroughly check their slips.

"There could be a very exciting Bank Holiday weekend ahead for one EuroMillions player in Limerick who is now holding a €500,000 winning ticket," Monaghan said, urging the winner to sign the back of their ticket, keep it safe, and contact the National Lottery prize claims team to arrange collecting their substantial sum.

As celebrations begin to unfold across the region, this latest win brings a welcome dose of joy and optimism to the local community. It serves as a timely reminder of the exciting possibilities that await players right here in Limerick, adding an extra layer of festive cheer to the long weekend festivities.
9307685.pullQuote: There could be a very exciting Bank Holiday weekend ahead for one EuroMillions player in Limerick who is now holding a €500,000 winning ticket.
9307685.localAngle: A Limerick resident is celebrating a massive €500,000 EuroMillions win just ahead of the Bank Holiday weekend.
9307685.originalTitle: ‘Check your tickets carefully!’: Limerick player has ‘incredible’ EuroMillions win

9307767.headline: Wedding Bells and All-Ireland Thrills: Limerick Hurling Star Ties the Knot
9307767.subheadline: Tributes pour in from across the county as one of Treaty County's most celebrated wing-forwards begins a new chapter.
9307767.story:
There was celebration across the Treaty County this weekend as one of Limerick hurling's most decorated wing-forwards officially tied the knot. The star player, who has proudly secured six All-Ireland medals and three prestigious All-Star awards during his illustrious career on the pitch, exchanged vows with his partner, Elaine—affectionately known to family and friends as Lainey—surrounded by loved ones.

The couple's love story began years ago on a memorable night out in Limerick, blossoming into a partnership that has now reached this joyful milestone. Supporters, teammates, and local community members have flooded social media and local forums with heartfelt messages of congratulations, celebrating not only his athletic achievements but also this important personal milestone for the couple.

While the hurling season may be paused, the pride of Limerick remains as strong as ever for one of its favorite sporting sons. As the newlyweds embark on this exciting new chapter together, the entire community joins in wishing them a lifetime of happiness, health, and shared success off the field.
9307767.pullQuote: The couple, who first met on a night out, received warm wishes from supporters across the county as they celebrated their wedding day.
9307767.localAngle: A legendary Limerick hurling star celebrates his wedding day, drawing warm wishes from supporters and sports fans across the county.
9307767.originalTitle: Limerick hurling star receives heartfelt best wishes on his wedding day

9307849.headline: Monagea Complete Inspiring Return with County Junior Hurling Triumph
9307849.subheadline: Resilient club secures immediate promotion back to Premier Junior 'A' ranks following commanding final performance
9307849.story:
Monagea capped off a remarkable season of resilience and dedication this weekend, claiming the Limerick Junior 'A' hurling title with a decisive victory over Killeedy. The triumph marks a proud milestone for the club and its supporters, coming exactly twelve years—and one hard-fought year of rebuilding—after their relegation from the higher grade. 

From the opening whistle, Monagea displayed the focus and teamwork that has defined their campaign throughout the county championship. Displaying clinical accuracy and unwavering defensive discipline, they managed to outpace a determined Killeedy side. Every player on the field contributed to a collective performance that reflected the depth of talent and community spirit thriving within the club.

The victory ensures an immediate return to the Premier Junior 'A' championship, a testament to the hard work put in by players, coaches, and the wider Monagea community behind the scenes. Rather than letting last year's setback define them, the club used the experience to strengthen their resolve, investing heavily in youth development and senior training alike.

As celebrations echo across the parish, the focus will soon turn to the challenges and excitement of competing in the higher tier next season. For now, however, Monagea can take immense pride in a championship performance that highlights the enduring strength and competitive spirit of Limerick club hurling at its finest.
9307849.pullQuote: The win sees Monagea promoted back to Premier Junior ‘A’ one year after being relegated from the same grade.
9307849.localAngle: This thrilling county final victory secures Monagea's immediate return to the Premier Junior 'A' grade, energizing the local community and setting the stage for an exciting 2027 hurling season in Limerick.
9307849.originalTitle: Monagea too strong for Killeedy in Limerick Junior 'A' hurling final

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.headline: Council Trials Innovative 'Zero Gravity' Mower to Boost Limerick's Biodiversity and Cut Emissions
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.subheadline: New machinery trial paves the way for sustainable meadow management across the county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.story:
Limerick City and County Council has successfully completed a trial of an advanced 'zero gravity' mowing system designed to enhance local biodiversity and support the county's climate action objectives. The specialized GHS Drive 1800 machine was leased for a pilot program focusing on grasslands and pollinator-friendly meadows within the Limerick Decarbonisation Zone and surrounding areas.

Unlike traditional mowing equipment, the innovative machine cuts and removes vegetation in a single, highly efficient operation. Environmental experts emphasize that removing grass cuttings is a vital best-practice technique for meadow management, as it reduces soil fertility and creates the optimal conditions for native wildflowers and pollinators to thrive. The successful trial aligns directly with the local authority's commitments under the Limerick Biodiversity Action Plan, the Climate Action Plan, and the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan.

Beyond its ecological benefits, the pilot highlighted significant operational advantages for the local authority. The machinery demonstrated reduced fuel consumption, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and a quieter operation compared to conventional equipment. Furthermore, research indicates that properly managed wildflower meadows encourage deeper root systems and increased soil carbon storage, gradually transforming local green spaces into valuable carbon sinks.

Building on the positive outcomes of the lease program, Limerick City and County Council is now exploring the permanent acquisition of similar technology. The move marks another proactive step in the region's long-term approach to sustainable open space management, ensuring that Limerick continues to lead by example in local environmental stewardship.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.pullQuote: Removing cuttings from meadows is recognised as a best-practice management technique, creating the conditions needed for a greater diversity of native wildflowers and pollinators to thrive.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.localAngle: The trial of the zero-gravity mower within the Limerick Decarbonisation Zone demonstrates the local authority's ongoing commitment to meeting county-wide climate action and biodiversity targets.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.originalTitle: Zero gravity machine hitting heights in biodiversity

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.headline: Abbeyfeale Property Transfer Sparks Healthy Debate on Local Development Strategy
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.subheadline: Elected members weigh in on proposed housing initiative involving Limerick Twenty Thirty
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.story:
Elected representatives in West Limerick are engaging in constructive discussions regarding a visionary proposal to allocate six council-owned properties in Abbeyfeale to Limerick Twenty Thirty. Unveiled at the October Newcastle West district meeting, the initiative aims to breathe new life into local housing stock, offering a sustainable, cost-recovery rental model tailored for working households and key workers in the area.

The properties—located at Convent Road, Colbert Terrace, Old Church Street, and the Bridge Inn—include a mix of one, two, three, and four-bedroom homes. Refurbished to an exceptionally high standard, these Grade A residences are expected to be ready by mid-November. Supporters of the project, including District Cathaoirleach Cllr Liam Galvin, highlight that bringing these previously idle buildings back into active use addresses a long-standing community priority and will significantly strengthen local spending power and economic sustainability in West Limerick.

At the same time, councillors are proactively examining the broader implications of utilizing a project development company traditionally focused on commercial growth for residential schemes. Fianna Fáil councillor Michael Collins raised important questions during the district meeting regarding the distinction between commercial and private housing mandates, calling for a dedicated workshop to ensure all elected members can collaborate on the optimal path forward. District leaders remain committed to open dialogue, balancing the urgent need to activate local housing with strategic planning for the county's long-term commercial vitality.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.pullQuote: I believe we will have them ready by the middle of November. I wasn’t 100 per cent in favour of the scheme that the Mayor was proposing but I am willing to give it a chance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.localAngle: The proposed disposal of Abbeyfeale council properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty marks a pivotal step in shaping the future of housing and economic development across West Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.originalTitle: Proposed disposal of Abbeyfeale properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty raises serious questions

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.headline: Limerick Property Market Shows Steady Growth with Rising Inventory and Slower Inflation Rates
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.subheadline: Latest MyHome report highlights positive trends for local homebuyers as market supply improves across the county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.story:
Property prices in Limerick have seen a steady annual increase of €10,000, bringing the median asking price across the county to €290,000, according to the latest MyHome Property Price Report for the third quarter of 2026. While the figures reflect continuous growth over the past year, asking prices remained flat over the final quarter, pointing to a stabilizing market environment for local buyers and sellers alike.

Specific property categories across the county have experienced varied shifts. Asking prices for three-bed semi-detached homes rose by €15,000 over the past year to reach €295,000, which includes a modest €5,000 increase in the third quarter alone. Meanwhile, four-bed semi-detached houses saw a decrease of €5,500 annually to settle at a median asking price of €359,500, despite experiencing a €7,000 rise during the most recent quarter. Market activity has also seen encouraging improvements, with 444 properties listed for sale in Limerick at the close of the third quarter—marking a 4 per cent increase over the period. Properties are currently going sale agreed in just under three months on average.

Industry experts have welcomed these developments as encouraging signs for the local housing market. Conall MacCoille, Chief Economist at Bank of Ireland, highlighted that the slowing rate of asking price inflation, combined with an increasing number of properties for sale and a pickup in homebuilding, creates a more favorable environment for prospective buyers. Additionally, MyHome Managing Director Joanne Geary pointed to strong engagement from first-time buyers, noting that first-time buyer transactions have risen by 12 per cent year-on-year, reflecting continued confidence and accessibility in Limerick's property sector.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.pullQuote: The rate of asking price inflation continues to slow, the number of properties for sale on MyHome is rising, and homebuilding has picked up.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.localAngle: The latest MyHome Property Price Report provides local readers with a comprehensive look at median asking prices, inventory levels, and housing market trends across Limerick county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.originalTitle: Limerick property prices continue to rise according to new report

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.headline: Terror and Talent Set for the Belltable as 'Big Shots Halloween Screams' Returns to Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.subheadline: Ireland's premier all-island horror film competition is back on Treaty City screens this Halloween night with original short films, live audiences, and cash prizes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.story:
Film enthusiasts and horror fans across Limerick are in for a spine-chilling treat next weekend as the Belltable prepares to host the return of 'Big Shots Halloween Screams' on Saturday, October 31. Following successful runs in 2024 and 2025, Ireland’s All-Island Horror Film Competition is once again bringing its unique brand of cinematic terror to the heart of the city, offering local audiences a front-row seat to some of the freshest talent in independent filmmaking.

Throughout the month of October, creative teams from every corner of the island have been hard at work writing, shooting, and editing their own original short horror films. These homegrown productions will culminate in a special live screening event at the Belltable, where audiences can experience the suspense together on the big screen. In addition to the thrill of the premiere, participating filmmakers will be competing for a range of prestigious awards and cash prizes.

Doors for the Halloween night event will open at 6.30pm, with the screenings set to kick off at 7.30pm. Tickets are available now for €12.50, offering an affordable and entertaining evening out for local culture seekers and horror aficionados alike. As cultural events continue to thrive in Limerick, the return of Big Shots Halloween Screams highlights the city's vibrant arts community and provides an exciting platform for emerging cinematic storytellers to showcase their craft.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.pullQuote: Teams from across the island will write, shoot and edit original short horror films throughout October for the live Belltable screening.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.localAngle: The popular all-island horror film competition returns to Limerick's Belltable venue, offering local film fans a thrilling Halloween night out.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.originalTitle: Big Shots Halloween Screams returns to Belltable for another night of frights

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.headline: Youth-Led LASTA ‘26 Festival Brings Fresh Energy and Creativity to the Belltable Stage
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.subheadline: Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca invite Limerick audiences to celebrate young artistic talent in a dynamic two-event programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.story:
The Belltable is set to come alive with youthful creativity and vibrant performances later this month as it hosts LASTA ‘26, a nationwide festival spearheaded by the Young Curators national mentorship programme. Local culture enthusiasts and young audiences alike are in for a treat as co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca unveil a diverse programme designed to transform the iconic Limerick venue into a welcoming space for artistic experimentation and community connection.

The festival kicks off on Wednesday, October 28, with two screenings of the timeless workplace comedy 9 to 5, scheduled for 5pm and 7.30pm. Presented personally by Ms. Luca and Mr. Cropper, the screenings serve as a special tribute to the legendary 1980 film starring Dolly Parton, Lily Tomlin, and Jane Fonda. Tickets for the cinematic event are affordably priced at €8 general admission and €5 concession, offering an accessible evening out for film fans across the city.

The excitement continues on Friday, October 30, at 7.30pm with 'Nighttime Medley', an intimate variety show that promises an unforgettable evening of performance, drag clowning, and contemporary dance. Billed as a celebration of mischief-makers and bold artistry, the line-up features acclaimed Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova—an Associate Artist at Dance Limerick—alongside Dublin-based performer Day Magee and rising drag clown sensation Whimsy. Ms. Vostokova will present her thought-provoking piece Pit, commissioned by Coisceim Dance Theatre, which explores the impact of modern urbanism through powerful choreography.

Events like LASTA ‘26 highlight the vital role that young people play in shaping Limerick’s vibrant cultural landscape. By providing a platform for emerging artists and welcoming peers into the heart of the city's arts scene, the festival reinforces the Belltable's position as a dynamic hub for community engagement, inspiration, and creative expression.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.pullQuote: Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca have put together a programme that welcomes their peers into the venue as a space for creative experimentation and fun.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.localAngle: Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova will perform her acclaimed piece 'Pit' at the Belltable as part of the nationwide LASTA '26 festival.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.originalTitle: Young curators bring LASTA ‘26 to Belltable with film screening and variety show

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.headline: Boost for Mid-West Healthcare as Dr Hammad Danish Joins UHL Respiratory Team
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.subheadline: New specialist appointment brings advanced expertise in non-invasive ventilation and pleural procedures to University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.story:
University Hospital Limerick (UHL) has bolstered its medical team with the appointment of Dr Hammad Danish as Consultant Respiratory Physician. The addition of Dr Danish is expected to bring a significant enhancement to respiratory healthcare services for patients throughout Limerick, Clare, and Tipperary, reinforcing the hospital's capacity to deliver specialized care locally.

Dr Danish brings specialized expertise in advanced procedures, including bronchoscopy and pleural management, alongside crucial experience in the care of patients requiring non-invasive ventilation. Hospital representatives highlighted that his specialized skill set will play a vital role in addressing regional healthcare needs and improving patient pathways across the Mid West.

Speaking on his arrival, Dr Danish expressed enthusiasm for his new role within the Limerick-based health service. "I am pleased to begin work at University Hospital Limerick and to join a dedicated team committed to delivering high-quality respiratory care across the region," he stated. "I am particularly excited by the prospect of contributing to the further development of respiratory services, supporting timely diagnosis, effective treatment and delivering better patient outcomes for those living with various respiratory conditions."

This appointment marks another positive step forward for healthcare provision in the region, reflecting ongoing efforts to expand specialist services and enhance patient care standards at UHL. Local healthcare advocates have welcomed the addition, noting that expanded clinical expertise directly benefits families and individuals managing chronic respiratory conditions in the community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.pullQuote: I am particularly excited by the prospect of contributing to the further development of respiratory services, supporting timely diagnosis, effective treatment and delivering better patient outcomes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.localAngle: The appointment of Dr Hammad Danish brings advanced respiratory expertise directly to University Hospital Limerick, improving specialist healthcare access for patients across the entire Mid West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362476.originalTitle: New Respiratory consultant appointed at UHL

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.headline: Digital Etiquette in Focus: Local HR Experts Urge Clarity on Workplace Chat Apps
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.subheadline: As WhatsApp and team messaging become staples of the modern working day, Limerick professionals are being reminded of the lasting impact of casual online conversations.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.story:
With messaging platforms like WhatsApp and team collaboration tools now deeply embedded in daily routines across Limerick, local employment specialists are highlighting the importance of maintaining professional standards online. While these tools offer speed and efficiency for businesses and workers alike, experts note that the casual nature of digital chats can sometimes lead to misunderstandings when messages are taken out of context during workplace reviews.

HR Hub, an O’Connell Street-based employment law and human resource management firm, emphasizes that digital communication connected to colleagues or business matters often falls within the scope of workplace conduct, regardless of when or where it was sent. Conversations that bridge personal and professional hours, or messages shared within smaller group chats, can easily circulate more widely through screenshots if disputes or complaints arise.

Rather than pointing toward heavy-handed monitoring, industry advisors suggest that fostering clear expectations is the most constructive way forward for local workplaces. By encouraging mindful communication—such as treating digital messages with the same care as spoken word—organizations across Limerick can help protect professional reputations while maintaining positive, collaborative environments.

Ultimately, experts view this as an opportunity for local businesses to reinforce communication guidelines that empower employees and managers alike. By championing best practices in digital correspondence, Limerick workplaces continue to build resilient, transparent, and supportive environments where modern technology enhances rather than complicates working relationships.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.pullQuote: The medium may have changed, but the standard has not — messages are quick, but the impact lasts beyond the message.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.localAngle: The guidance is provided by Limerick-based HR Hub, offering expert advice tailored to local businesses and professionals navigating modern workplace challenges.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.originalTitle: Employment Matters: When WhatsApp messages become workplace evidence

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.headline: Mid-West Business Excellence in Spotlight as Limerick Chamber Reveals 15th Annual Awards Shortlist
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.subheadline: Finalists ranging from emerging enterprises to established community leaders set to be honored at next month's gala at the Limerick Strand Hotel.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.story:
The dynamic spirit of enterprise across the Mid-West is taking center stage following the announcement of the shortlist for the 15th annual Limerick Chamber Regional Business Awards. Sponsored by the Technological University of the Shannon (TUS), this year's finalists highlight a diverse cross-section of the local economy, spanning innovative startups, established SMEs, and dedicated community and not-for-profit organizations.

The highly anticipated winners will be revealed on Friday, November 13, during the Limerick Chamber President’s Dinner and Regional Business Awards ceremony at the Limerick Strand Hotel. Senior business leaders and regional stakeholders from across Limerick and the wider region will gather for the gala event to celebrate local commercial success and resilience.

Limerick Chamber President Maria Gleeson praised the calibre of the shortlisted organizations, noting the exceptional breadth of talent and innovation driving the regional economy forward. Echoing this sentiment, TUS Vice President Liam Brown emphasized the vital synergy between education, enterprise, and industry in shaping a competitive future for the Mid-West.

Among the many notable contenders across categories such as environmental excellence, digital transformation, and customer experience are local fixtures like Croom Medical, Mother Macs, University Concert Hall, and Hook & Ladder. These organizations demonstrate the ongoing dedication to growth, community impact, and employment excellence that continues to strengthen the local business landscape.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.pullQuote: What stands out each year is the breadth of talent and enterprise across the Mid-West.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.localAngle: The annual Limerick Chamber Regional Business Awards celebrate the homegrown businesses, employers, and community initiatives driving economic success and resilience across Limerick and the Mid-West.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362449.headline: Mid West Health Authorities Urge Early Vaccination as HSE Launches Winter Campaign Following 30 Local Flu Deaths
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362449.subheadline: Free flu and COVID-19 jabs are now available across Limerick, Clare, and North Tipperary pharmacies and GP surgeries to protect vulnerable residents.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362449.story:
As the colder months approach, health officials across the Mid West are calling on the community to bolster their defenses against seasonal illnesses with the official launch of the HSE’s Winter Vaccination Programme. The proactive campaign comes on the heels of sobering figures from last winter, which saw 1,780 confirmed cases of influenza reported across Limerick, Clare, and North Tipperary, resulting in 30 tragic deaths in the region.

Local health data highlights the significant impact the virus had on local healthcare infrastructure last year, with 839 individuals requiring hospital treatment and 11 patients admitted to intensive care units. In response to these challenges, medical professionals and community leaders are championing a strong preventive approach this season, emphasizing that vaccines remain the most effective tool to safeguard community health, ease pressure on local hospitals, and protect our most vulnerable neighbours.

To ensure widespread protection, both the flu and COVID-19 vaccines are now available free of charge to eligible groups at participating GPs and pharmacies. Recommendations target everyone aged 60 and older, individuals with underlying medical conditions, pregnant women, healthcare workers, and children aged two to 17—the latter of whom can avail of a convenient, needle-free nasal spray. Dedicated HSE vaccination teams are also coordinating closely with local nursing homes to deliver vaccines directly to residents, ensuring seamless access for those with mobility needs.

Medical experts note that it takes approximately two weeks for the vaccines to provide full immunity, making the current window ideal for getting jabbed before peak flu season arrives. By taking up the offer of vaccination early, Limerick residents can play a vital role in fostering a resilient, healthy community capable of weathering the winter months safely together.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362449.pullQuote: Last winter, a total of 1,780 confirmed cases of flu were reported in the Mid West, with 839 people hospitalised.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362449.localAngle: The HSE Winter Vaccination Programme directly impacts Limerick residents by providing free, accessible flu and COVID-19 vaccines through local GPs and pharmacies to protect the regional community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362449.originalTitle: 80 deaths last year among flu victims in Mid West

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.headline: Limerick's Own Master Magician Steve Spade to Channel Houdini at Bunratty Castle This Bank Holiday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.subheadline: A century after the legendary escapologist's passing, Bunratty Castle and Folk Park promises a weekend of family-friendly thrills, magic, and historical spectacle.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.story:
As communities across the region prepare for the Halloween festivities this bank holiday weekend, Bunratty Castle and Folk Park is set to offer an unforgettable experience blending history, illusion, and local talent. Marking a century since the passing of legendary escapologist Harry Houdini, Limerick’s own master magician Steve Spade is stepping up to channel the spirit and skill of the historic icon in a series of live performances.

Affectionately known as the Irish Houdini—a title earned in part after winning a set of the master's own handcuffs during a rope-tie challenge on the Discovery Channel—Spade's appearance promises to be a highlight of the weekend. Alongside death-defying escape recreations, visitors can look forward to traditional parlour magic, masterful illusions, and an engaging question-and-answer session exploring Houdini’s enduring legacy.

Beyond the headline magic acts, the historic site will come alive with an array of family-friendly entertainment designed to delight visitors of all ages. Guests can encounter the captivating Human Spider illusion, marvel at Vera the Velociraptor alongside her daring trainer in the Folk Park streets, and participate in traditional Halloween activities such as apple bobbing in the Golden Vale. Roaming performers, including international contortionist and juggler Frederico Fandango, will ensure that the festive community spirit is felt around every corner of the park.

With interactive attractions ranging from the whimsical Ghost Recruitment Bureau to lively theatrical performances like the Witch Trial, Bunratty’s Halloween lineup offers a wonderful opportunity for families and visitors to celebrate the season together. The event highlights the vibrant cultural energy of the region, showcasing world-class local artistry while providing a welcoming and uplifting space for community celebration.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.pullQuote: "Houdini was much more than an escape artist. He was also a master magician and a parlour performer..."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.localAngle: Limerick master magician Steve Spade is headlining the bank holiday weekend events at Bunratty Castle, channeling the legendary Harry Houdini.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.originalTitle: Spirit of Houdini will be one of the friendly ghosts to haunt Bunratty this weekend

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.headline: Limerick Mental Health Professional Calls for Rigorous Standards Amid Proposed Training Changes
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.subheadline: Local expert Trish Murphy champions high-quality care to ensure vulnerable individuals receive the dedicated support they deserve.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.story:
As mental health services across the country continue to adapt to growing demands, a prominent Limerick psychotherapist is advocating for uncompromising standards in practitioner training. Following the recent annual conference of the Irish Council for Psychotherapy (ICP), Limerick native Trish Murphy has raised important questions regarding proposed regulatory changes by CORU, the health and social care professionals regulator. While the proposals aim to address existing waiting lists by streamlining the qualification process, mental health advocates emphasize the vital importance of maintaining comprehensive training frameworks that prioritize deep therapeutic relationships.

Ms. Murphy, currently the Director of Student Counselling Services at Trinity College Dublin and an experienced practitioner with deep roots in Limerick, highlighted the critical need for robust clinical preparation. The discussion centers on ensuring that future psychotherapists are fully equipped with the relational capacity required to support children, adolescents, and adults navigating complex trauma. Industry professionals stress that comprehensive training, including personal therapy and supervised practice, remains a cornerstone of safe, effective, and compassionate mental health care.

The Irish Council for Psychotherapy has expressed a strong desire to collaborate constructively with regulatory bodies to achieve shared goals of public protection and service accessibility. By fostering open dialogue between regulatory authorities and professional organizations, the mental health community is working proactively to build a resilient, high-standard framework. Through continued cooperation and a shared commitment to excellence, stakeholders across the sector are striving to ensure that Limerick residents and individuals nationwide continue to have access to safe, professional, and empowering mental health support systems.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.pullQuote: Newly trained psychotherapists will not be equipped to provide the relational capacity that is essential to the long-term processing of trauma.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.localAngle: Limerick-born psychotherapist Trish Murphy is leading the national conversation on safeguarding the quality of mental health training and protecting vulnerable clients.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.originalTitle: Limerick psychotherapist warns of dangers of fast-track training

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.headline: Limerick Education Community Rallies in Support Following Glenstal Abbey Closure Announcement
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.subheadline: Local schools offer solidarity and reflect on a rich 94-year history as the region processes the planned wind-down of the iconic institution.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.story:
The Limerick education community has come together in a strong display of solidarity following last week's unexpected announcement regarding the future of Glenstal Abbey School. Educational institutions across the city and county have been quick to offer their support and share fond reflections as the historic school prepares for a phased closure no later than August 2028.

Villiers Secondary School on the North Circular Road was among the first to respond, publishing a heartfelt statement that highlighted the deep historical ties between the two institutions. Noting their shared heritage linked through the Barrington family lands and buildings, Villiers acknowledged the profound impact of the news on students, families, and staff. As fellow educators and neighbours, Villiers emphasized the enduring legacy Glenstal has built since opening its doors in 1932, serving generations of boys aged 12 to 18 across the region.

St. Munchin’s College on the Corbally Road also extended its warmest thoughts via social media, reaching out to the entire Glenstal community, including past pupils, parents, teachers, and the Benedictine monks. https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.headline: Double-Whammy Weather: Limerick Prepares as Storm Boelo Follows Fast on Heels of Austen
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.subheadline: Met Éireann issues back-to-back Status Yellow warnings for wind and rain as the county braces for severe gusts and difficult travelling conditions.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.story:
Limerick is preparing to weather another Atlantic system this weekend as Storm Boelo sweeps across the country in the early hours of Saturday morning. Coming just days after Storm Austen passed over the region last Thursday evening, this latest front brings a fresh test of local infrastructure and community resilience as the second named storm of the season arrives.

Met Éireann has put dual Status Yellow warnings in place for Limerick. A heavy rain warning comes into effect at 4am on Saturday, running until 3pm, to be immediately followed by a wind warning from 1pm Saturday through to midday Sunday. Forecasters are warning of severe and damaging gusts that could bring localized disruption to homes, businesses, and public transport networks, alongside potential flooding in vulnerable spots.

Speaking on RTÉ’s Morning Ireland, Met Éireann senior forecaster Gerry Murphy noted that Storm Boelo differs in trajectory from its predecessor by tracking to the north of the country. "From after midnight tonight, we will see heavy rain developing in the west and that’s going to sweep quickly across the country, bringing very wet and windy weather as we go through tomorrow," Murphy said.

Despite the challenging conditions ahead, local authorities and communities across Treaty County are well-practiced in pulling together during severe weather events. Residents and event organizers are encouraged to secure outdoor property, check in on vulnerable neighbors, and allow extra time for weekend journeys as Limerick navigates the latest test of the winter season with its characteristic community spirit.
